title: DynamicVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
claim: Prior systems block between inference and execution, causing stale actions; ours streams actions continuously, and a new benchmark supports evaluating this.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked timelines on top, wide benchmark panel below; timeline contrast
description: The top row has two timeline diagrams. Panel (a) shows current VLA models. Rounded pills hold observation and action IDs, with robot camera frames beneath them. Blue brackets mark 'Model Infer' and 'Action Execute' phases, and a 'P.E. Gap' arrow marks the delay before each action chunk. Panel (b) shows DynamicVLA. Its chunks overlap, and 'LAAS' arrows link observations to later action chunks, with dashed pills for omitted items. A legend sits under each timeline. The bottom panel (c) describes the DOM benchmark. On the left is a radar chart comparing π0.5, SmolVLA, VLASH and DynamicVLA across nine skills. In the middle is a 3x3 grid of scene photos grouped as Interaction, Perception and Generalization. On the right is a data-collection pipeline, with Isaac Sim and real-world sources and 200K and 2K episode statistics. Blue and green dominate the colors.
caption: (a) Current VLA models suffer from inter-chunk waiting and perception--execution (P.E.) mismatch, leading to delayed or misaligned reactions to moving objects. (b) \OM uses a continuous inference schedule to maintain a non-blocking action stream, while LAAS discards latency-invalid prefixes and executes only temporally valid suffixes to preserve action-time alignment under dynamic object motion. (c) The \OD (\ODslug) benchmark features 2.8K scenes and 206 objects for evaluating Perception, Interaction, and Generalization, while its data collection pipeline enables gathering of 200K synthetic and 2K real-world episodes.
abstract: Manipulating dynamic objects remains an open challenge for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models. Although recent VLAs generalize well in static manipulation, dynamic scenes introduce a latency-induced perception-execution mismatch: object states continue to evolve during inference, making actions predicted from past observations stale at execution time. We present DynamicVLA, a latency-aware VLA model for dynamic object manipulation. It combines a compact 0.4B architecture and convolutional vision encoder for efficient multimodal inference with a continuous inference schedule that overlaps reasoning and execution for non-blocking control. Latent-aware Action Streaming then discards latency-invalid action prefixes and executes only the temporally valid suffix of each predicted chunk, preserving action-time alignment under dynamic object motion. To fill the missing foundation of dynamic manipulation data, we introduce the Dynamic Object Manipulation (DOM) benchmark, built with an automated collection pipeline that gathers 200K synthetic episodes across 2.8K scenes and 206 objects, and enables fast collection of 2K real-world episodes without teleoperation. Extensive evaluations in simulation and on real robots show that DynamicVLA improves dynamic manipulation success under changing object motion, perception-heavy instructions, and unseen motion patterns.
